title: DEXTER: Diffusion-Guided EXplanations with TExtual Reasoning for Vision Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating classifiers trained on datasets with natural or injected gender skews (CelebA for blonde classification, FairFaces for age classification). The paper uses the proposed DEXTER framework to generate class-maximizing images, which are then captioned and summarized by an LLM into textual bias reports. These reports are evaluated for accuracy and consistency by human annotators and LLM-as-a-judge metrics.

Assessing spurious background correlations using the Waterbirds dataset (bird species vs. land/water backgrounds) and SalientImageNet. The methodology involves optimizing text prompts to synthesize images that strongly activate a target classifier, discovering words associated with these visual slices, and evaluating the model's reliance on irrelevant background contexts.

Using LLM-generated textual reasoning to analyze the representations of age groups (20-29 vs 50-59 years old) in facial classifiers trained on FairFaces, identifying the model's reliance on societal stereotypes such as neutral/serious expressions for older individuals or specific idealized facial features for youth.

Qualitatively analyzing LLM-generated bias reports for facial classifiers (FairFaces) to surface the model's disproportionate reliance on specific skin tones (e.g., light or medium brown) when predicting demographic classes.
